pencereler.0-5: A single skier can bring down thousands of tons of snow. It explodes downhill
pencereler.5-12: at eighty miles an hour. The slope was not the problem. The danger was hidden underneath. Snow falls in
pencereler.12-20: layers all winter long. Between them sits a weak, sugary layer of crystals. It holds the slab above like a house of
pencereler.20-30: cards. One extra load snaps that bond and the slab slides. Slopes near thirty eight degrees are the most dangerous.

segmentler.metin: A single skier can bring down thousands of tons of snow.
It took only a single skier.
The answer is weak-layer collapse under a snow slab — and it is why avalanche forecasting tracks buried weak layers all winter.
